_readme: Every drag and gesture this app has, declared beside the non-drag control that satisfies it (Doctrine §4, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 and SC 2.5.1). tools/interactions-check.mjs holds the structure: a declared drag with no alternative fails the build, and so does a declaration naming a surface that does not exist. The live half — that each selector actually matches in a booted app — is asserted by tools/a11y.mjs, which is the only thing that can press them.

interactions.what: Dragging a job card from its grip into another column, and to a position within that column.
interactions.note: Started by movement past an 8px threshold, never by a press-and-hold. touch-action: none is set on the grip only, so the board still scrolls everywhere else.

alternative.what: The Move button on every card opens a list that answers BOTH halves of the drag: a named position within this column ("Put before Calibration cube", "Put last in Printing") and every other column. This is the path keyboard and assistive technology use, and it is what makes the drag an enhancement rather than a requirement. It listed only the columns until 0.3.0, so the ORDER of a column was reachable by drag and by nothing else — a gap this file described accurately in `what` and did not describe in `alternative`, and which no gate can see, because a gate can tell that an alternative exists and not that it does less than the drag it stands in for.

interactions.what: Scrolling the board sideways to reach a column that is off screen.
interactions.note: Native scrolling in one direction, with no custom handler. Reachable from a keyboard because every control inside the board is focusable and focusing one scrolls it into view.

alternative.what: A card can be moved to any column without the target column ever being on screen, using the Move list.
